## Declaration

The executable declaration is `count_mixture_lowpass/declaration.R`. It is
committed before the campaign it judges. This is a **chr20 point-estimation
and interval-calibration check**, not whole-genome release evidence.

The registered phased 1000G chr20 source, founder pedigree and matched sites
supply linked haplotypes. Sixty CEU and sixty YRI founders are drawn without
replacement with seed 332202610. Each replicate draws distinct founders:
two CEU haplotypes form the sample, two other CEU haplotypes form a
same-population second genome, or two YRI haplotypes form an other-population
second genome. An IBD1 second genome transmits one complete phased haplotype
of the sample and takes its other haplotype from a distinct CEU founder.
Frequencies are the called phased allele frequencies among all founders of
the corresponding population, clamped to [0.001, 0.999]. Founder labels
exclude pedigree descendants; residual relatedness is not independently
screened. Linkage is retained across sites; no genotype-independent SNP
simulation substitutes for phased genomes.

There are 50 replicates in each of 108 primary strata: three relationships,
shares 0/0.01/0.02/0.05/0.10/0.20, depths 0.1/0.2/0.4, and fixed errors
0.0001/0.0002. Depth is Poisson. A fragment independently chooses a source,
then one of its alleles, then has symmetric sequencing error. Equivalently,
ALT is binomial conditional on the two phased dosages. With probability
0.002 a site's ALT count is uniform on 0..depth. Excess homozygosity is zero.
The fitting calibration equals these generating parameters. Matched IBD1
and unrelated hypotheses remain separate conditional fits, not relationship
classification. Blocks are **1 Mb on chr20**, to reach the unchanged
30-informative-block interval floor; no 10 Mb whole-genome precision claim
is made. All statuses, missing intervals and failed fits remain denominators.

The three registered 30x chr20 count tables are thinned at 1/300, 1/150 and
1/75, both as single sources and as ordered two-source combinations at each
nonzero share. Ref and ALT counts are independently binomial-thinned, not
reads or templates. The nominal share is the thinning probability share,
not necessarily the realized fragment share when source depths differ.
Each stratum has 50 draws, fixed error 0.00015, artefact weight 0.002 and
zero excess homozygosity. These are calibration-transfer diagnostics, not
known-truth accuracy gates. Single-source baseline offsets are retained.

### Frozen criteria

Release targets from the design require at least 200 independent replicates
per primary stratum on a genome-wide linked reference. With 50 chr20 draws
these targets are **not evaluated as release gates**, even where a numerical
threshold is met. Observed thresholds are shown separately:

* For correctly specified interior shares at least 0.05: absolute mean bias
  <= 0.005/0.0035/0.0025 at 0.1/0.2/0.4x.
* At least 90% have absolute error <= 0.020/0.014/0.010 for anchored
  other-population singles, <= 0.025/0.015/0.008 for matched unrelated,
  <= 0.050/0.025/0.015 for matched IBD1. Missing fits count as failures.
* Interior 95% interval coverage is 90–98%, counting missing intervals as
  uncovered. Zero-share positive claims use lower limit > 0; their one-sided
  exact 95% binomial upper bound must be <= 0.075. Missing intervals also
  have a separately reported denominator, not an inferred null claim.
* At least one replicate in every synthetic and thinning stratum has all
  native-input block moment sums independently reconstructed in R, with
  exact integer counters and relative error <= 1e-10 (absolute 1e-10 near
  zero). Every primary stratum's first replicate is also fitted at one and
  four threads: statuses must agree and shares and moments must agree to
  the same tolerance.
* Fresh processes, three repetitions each, scale sites 100k/200k/400k and
  sample-by-candidate groups 1/2/4. Peak RSS and DuckDB peak buffers must be
  <= 512 MiB overhead + 3 times modeled live state: 768 bytes per SQL input
  row plus 1024 bytes per physical native block and group. This explicitly
  includes SQL validation/join/sort state, not just bounded native moments.
  Memory limit is 3 GB, no spill. Timing exponent <= 1.25 at each doubling
  is evaluated only if the 1x query takes at least five seconds; smaller
  workloads report timing without a verdict. Input rows, output rows,
  elapsed time, spreads, buffers, RSS and spill remain visible.

The exploratory ordered/unordered/materialization comparison is reported
separately from the declared campaign. Same-population relationship
ambiguity, weak pairs, frequency mismatch and calibration transfer are
limitations, not reasons to drop observations.

## Execution and provenance

The campaign uses registered inputs only. From the repository root, with a
private library containing the current `duckhtsbench` registry:

```sh
taskset -c 0-5 Rscript benchmarks/count_mixture_lowpass/stage.R build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension
taskset -c 0-5 Rscript benchmarks/count_mixture_lowpass/run.R build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension /tmp/lowpass-campaign
```

`collect.R` reads the campaign, retained compensated-sum campaign and
exploratory memory probes, then writes the checked-in results. Recovery
workers run in three fresh R/DuckDB processes at a time, with one DuckDB
thread except the explicit four-thread comparison. Recovery timings are
not performance evidence. Scaling runs alone in fresh processes, one
DuckDB thread, three repetitions, six assigned CPU cores (0–5). Inputs
are warm cached; query elapsed time excludes startup, extension loading
and view creation. RSS includes those costs. DuckDB 3 GB memory limit and
no spill apply to the measured scaling queries. Source acquisition and
haplotype staging are outside measured queries.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
source("count_mixture_lowpass/declaration.R")
results_dir <- "count_mixture_lowpass/results"
read_result <- function(name) read.csv(file.path(results_dir, name))
metadata <- dget(file.path(results_dir, "metadata.txt"))
strata <- read_result("strata.csv")
primary <- strata[strata$kind == "synthetic", ]
thinning <- strata[strata$kind == "thinning", ]
```

```{r provenance, results='asis'}
cat("Campaign source revision: `", metadata$source_revision, "`.\n\n", sep = "")
cat(metadata$R, "; DuckDB R ", metadata$duckdb, ".\n\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(grep("Model name:|Socket\\(s\\):|CPU\\(s\\):", metadata$cpu_details, value = TRUE), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
cat("Native source and driver SHA-256 hashes and the loaded extension hash are retained in ",
    "[metadata.txt](count_mixture_lowpass/results/metadata.txt). The declaration was committed as `",
    metadata$declaration_commit, "` before the campaign.\n\n", sep = "")
cat("Synthetic: ", sum(primary$replicates), " replicates / ", nrow(primary), " strata; count thinning: ",
    sum(thinning$replicates), " replicates / ", nrow(thinning), " strata.\n", sep = "")
```

The phased source is the 1000G 3202-sample GRCh38 release of 2020-10-28,
chr20. Raw source and founder pedigree identities are pinned in the
registry. There are 108,757 matched sites and 120 selected founders in the
derived artifact `count_mixture_lowpass_chr20_haplotypes`. The three count
tables each contain 87,867 common chr20 sites; their canonical count hashes
are pinned in the registry. The network-free staging test checks temporary
cache isolation, phased decoding, population frequencies, repeat staging,
and failure on a missing raw input. Pedigree and phase are checked;
cryptic relatedness and individual-frequency agreement are not established.

## Criteria and numerical invariants

```{r criteria}
knitr::kable(read_result("summary.csv"))
```

The R oracle forms weighted cross-products and ALT/discordance moments from
the generated counts and frequencies, independently of the macro's SQL
expressions. It compares every block and every moment supplied to the
native fitter. Integer QC counters compare exactly. Native integer-limb
sum tests independently cover dyadic integer oracles, subnormals, merges,
round-to-even ties, sticky rounding, invalid inputs and capacity errors.

```{r numerical}
x <- read_result("oracle_and_threads.csv")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  datasets = nrow(x), max_R_relative_moment_error = max(x$moment_error),
  integer_counter_failures = sum(!x$counters_exact), status_failures = sum(!x$status_equal),
  max_thread_share_error = max(x$share_error), max_thread_moment_error = max(x$thread_moment_error)))
```

## Linked chr20 recovery

The primary point below is the conditional whole-fit `share`, not a
relationship selected by its score. Every stratum has 50 independent
random draws conditional on this fixed panel. Opposite conditional models
are also retained in the compressed replicate table. `conditional` counts
`ok_conditional` statuses; other statuses remain denominators. Mean bias
uses all finite reported shares (its count is retained in `strata.csv`). A
missing or non-conditional fit is a point-accuracy failure, and a missing
interval is uncovered. Wide or disconnected confidence sets are not
removed. `singles_mean`, `singles_bias` and `singles_within_limit_fraction`
retain the separate anchored read-only diagnostic for other-population
strata; they do not replace the declared whole-fit comparator.

```{r observed}
criteria_names <- c(bias = "bias_observed", accuracy = "accuracy_observed",
                    coverage = "coverage_observed", null = "null_observed")
observed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(criteria_names), function(name) {
  verdicts <- primary[[criteria_names[[name]]]]
  eligible <- verdicts != "not applicable"
  data.frame(criterion = name, strata = sum(eligible), met = sum(verdicts == "met"),
             failed = sum(verdicts == "fail"), incomplete = sum(verdicts == "incomplete"),
             release_verdict = "not evaluated: chr20, 50 < 200")
}))
knitr::kable(observed)
```

These numerical thresholds mostly **fail for point accuracy** on chr20.
Adequate-looking coverage can reflect wide intervals, not accurate shares.
At 0.1x this evidence does not establish dependable 1–2% share detection.
No universal detection limit is inferred. In particular, the matched IBD1
branch can have uninformative confidence sets and positive null estimates.
The 200-replicate genome-wide criteria are not passed by pooling depths,
errors, relationships or small-share strata. The whole-genome reference
has more sites and linkage blocks; chr20 results neither certify nor
refute its numerical targets.

```{r primary-strata}
knitr::kable(primary[c("id", "relationship", "depth", "seq_error", "truth", "conditional",
                       "mean_share", "bias", "accurate_fraction", "interval_coverage", "positive_claims")], digits = 4)
```

All per-stratum verdicts, missing-interval counts and exact one-sided null
bounds are in [strata.csv](count_mixture_lowpass/results/strata.csv).
The 50-draw binomial uncertainty is material: even zero observed positive
null claims has a one-sided 95% upper bound of about 0.058. Missing
intervals make the null verdict incomplete, rather than certifying the null criterion.

## Registered count thinning

```{r single-source}
knitr::kable(thinning[thinning$truth == 0,
  c("receiver", "depth", "replicates", "mean_share", "intervals", "positive_claims")], digits = 5)
```

Single-source offsets and missing intervals are retained. The largest
single-source mean share is about 0.0031 at nominal 0.1x. At higher depth,
several baseline fits concentrate at zero while intervals are unavailable.
These counts have empirical error and allele-specific depth, not the
synthetic generating calibration. The two-source share is nominal and
cannot be treated as exact truth without correcting for source coverage.
Thus two-source bias and coverage are diagnostics, not release gate passes.

```{r two-source}
knitr::kable(thinning[thinning$truth > 0,
  c("id", "receiver", "donor", "depth", "truth", "mean_share", "intervals", "positive_claims")], digits = 4)
```

## Scaling and memory

Each input row has two frequencies, three counts, position, sample,
candidate and chromosome. Sites use a generated numeric panel. Group
scaling is (samples,candidates) = (1,1), (2,1), (2,2), with shared counts
validated across candidates. The ranges fit within one 1 Mb block per
group: this measures SQL input scaling and bounded aggregation, **not**
chr20 interval fitting or scaling in the number of jackknife blocks.
Output denominators are conditional rows, not raw sites. The live-state
model and ceiling were frozen before the run. The 512 MiB overhead
allowance is conservative relative to the measured empty-process RSS:

```{r empty-process}
knitr::kable(read_result("empty_process.csv"), digits = 3)
```

```{r scaling}
knitr::kable(read_result("scaling_summary.csv"), digits = 3)
```

All 18 scaling runs satisfy RSS and DuckDB buffer ceilings without spill.
The 1x runs are shorter than five seconds, so the exponent gate is **not
evaluated**. The apparent exponents are descriptive, not a passed timing
criterion. Longer identical workloads and a multi-block timing workload
are still missing. Individual repetitions and modeled live-state bytes
are in [scaling.csv](count_mixture_lowpass/results/scaling.csv).

### Exploratory aggregate comparison

```{r exploratory-memory}
knitr::kable(read_result("exploratory_memory.csv"), digits = 3)
```

The ordered implementation was measured at `1c30c875`; its native sources
are unchanged in the current rebased counterpart `6e017d1c`.
These one-thread, single-run probes use the same numeric range workload as
scaling, but short identifier labels and one repetition rather than three;
they are exploratory comparisons, not a no-regression timing claim.
`unordered` is compensated `fsum` without raw materialization;
`materialized` is `fsum` with it. Explicit materialization increased peak
buffers and RSS in this comparison, so the macro uses `NOT MATERIALIZED`.
It still scans the relation repeatedly and SQL memory remains input-sized.

Ordered aggregates retained rows: at 400k sites their peak buffers were
855 MiB and RSS 578 MiB. The final exact-sum range workload uses fixed
152-byte integer-limb accumulators, rounded once to double; final peak
buffers and RSS are in the three-repeat table above. Native moments do not
retain sites. This is **not** a constant-memory claim for validation,
joins, window ordering or the entire query.

Compensated sums pass the moment tolerance but did not preserve the share
criterion near a floating objective minimum. The retained
[compensated-sum counterexamples](count_mixture_lowpass/results/compensated_sum_counterexamples.csv)
contain all 207 dataset checks, including 69 failed share comparisons
(maximum about 1.6e-7). They are not discarded to certify the final sums.
Exact sums preserve the fitter and the unchanged bitwise SQL regression.

## Retained evidence and scope

* [replicates.csv.gz](count_mixture_lowpass/results/replicates.csv.gz): all
  conditional fits, statuses, primary-model flags and principal diagnostics.
* [replicate_qc.csv.gz](count_mixture_lowpass/results/replicate_qc.csv.gz):
  all replicate input/output counters, pair denominators and shared singles,
  pair-residual and leverage diagnostics. Join on `(kind,id,replicate)`.
* [oracle_and_threads.csv](count_mixture_lowpass/results/oracle_and_threads.csv):
  every independently checked stratum, not only passing examples.

The approximately 1.3 MB result bundle retains failures as well as successes.
This campaign checks calibrated chr20 simulations and real count-thinning
transfer. It does not establish a genome-wide precision or detection limit,
arbitrary calibration robustness, sample-specific excess homozygosity,
relationship classification, or error calibration for arbitrary low-pass
inputs. No criterion is widened to obtain a pass.
